finding: Weeks with more ticket sales are weeks with fuller hotels (correlation 0.70).
check: Bootstrap of 156 weeks: 95% interval about 0.60 to 0.78.
limit: Summer and festivals raise both series; the data does not show that site visits fill hotels.

finding: The three festival months stood 18% to 29% above the seasonal baseline.
check: Baseline from the 2023 seasonal shape and the median yearly growth; all other months within 5% of it.
limit: Three festival months and one choice of baseline; other events in those months are not ruled out.

finding: Satisfaction rose in every origin market from 2024 to 2025 while the overall mean fell from 4.15 to 4.07.
check: Means by origin, and the 2025 mean recomputed at the 2024 mix of visitors (4.25).

finding: At the Honey Museum, weekend visitors were more satisfied than weekday visitors in 2025 (gap 0.30).
check: Largest of 27 site-year gaps; p = 0.03 taken alone; a gap that large appears among 27 in about half of shuffles.
limit: Found by searching 27 comparisons; to be tested on the 2026 survey before any announcement.

finding: Guided visits were rated about 0.4 point higher than unguided ones in 2025.
check: Question written down before the 2024 survey was opened; 2025 difference +0.39, interval +0.31 to +0.47.
limit: Visitors choose a guided visit; the data does not show that guiding causes the higher rating.
